# @byo-oss/entitlements

Plan entitlements as a better-auth plugin. A typed catalog of plans, features and limits; per-organization snapshot of the billing state, atomic usage counters and staff overrides, all in the app's own database (any better-auth adapter). Requires better-auth ^1.7.7 and the organization plugin. Organizations only: no user-scoped subscriptions.

## Install & wire

npm install @byo-oss/entitlements

Every sample below is complete and compiles as written. Paths in the first comment line show how the files import each other.

```ts
// lib/catalog.ts (browser-safe; also importable from a static pricing page)
import { defineEntitlements } from "@byo-oss/entitlements/catalog"

// every plan sets every key and nothing else (type error + boot error). Plan keys /^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$/.
// Limits: non-negative integers or "unlimited". At most 150 feature+limit keys.
// Never rename a plan key that has subscribers: alias it.
export const catalog = defineEntitlements({
  features: ["exports", "sso", "prioritySupport"],
  limits: {
    apiCalls: { kind: "metered", period: "day" }, // day | month (UTC) | billing (subscription period)
    members: { kind: "capacity" }, // the app supplies the count
    projects: { kind: "capacity" },
    retentionDays: { kind: "value" }, // a plan setting, read with getLimit
  },
  plans: {
    free: {
      features: { exports: false, sso: false, prioritySupport: false },
      limits: { apiCalls: 1_000, members: 5, projects: 3, retentionDays: 7 },
      display: { name: "Free" },
    },
    pro: {
      features: { exports: true, sso: false, prioritySupport: false },
      limits: { apiCalls: 50_000, members: 50, projects: "unlimited", retentionDays: 90 },
    },
  },
  defaultPlan: "free",
  planAliases: { legacy: "pro" },
})
```

```ts
// lib/permissions.ts
// access control: spread the statements, give roles the actions.
// "override" is only checked in the staff organization, "read" in the target organization (or the staff one).
import { createAccessControl } from "better-auth/plugins/access"
import { adminAc, defaultStatements, memberAc, ownerAc } from "better-auth/plugins/organization/access"
import { entitlementsStatements } from "@byo-oss/entitlements"

export const ac = createAccessControl({ ...defaultStatements, ...entitlementsStatements })
export const roles = {
  owner: ac.newRole({ ...ownerAc.statements, entitlements: ["read", "override"] }),
  admin: ac.newRole({ ...adminAc.statements, entitlements: ["read", "override"] }),
  member: ac.newRole({ ...memberAc.statements, entitlements: ["read"] }),
}
```

```ts
// lib/auth.ts
// organization() MUST come before entitlements(). Then: npx @better-auth/cli migrate
// (creates entitlementSnapshot, entitlementOverride, entitlementUsage).
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"
import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins/organization"
import { entitlements } from "@byo-oss/entitlements"
import { catalog } from "./catalog"
import { ac, roles } from "./permissions"

export const auth = betterAuth({
  plugins: [
    organization({ ac, roles }),
    // add source: fromBetterAuthStripe() under Billing sources
    entitlements({ catalog, staffOrganizationId: process.env.STAFF_ORGANIZATION_ID }),
  ],
})
```

```ts
// lib/auth-client.ts
import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/react"
import { organizationClient } from "better-auth/client/plugins"
import { entitlementsClient } from "@byo-oss/entitlements/client"

export const authClient = createAuthClient({
  plugins: [organizationClient(), entitlementsClient()],
})

export async function clientCalls(organizationId: string) {
  await authClient.entitlements.get({ query: { organizationId } })
  await authClient.entitlements.refresh({ organizationId })
  await authClient.entitlements.overrides({ query: { organizationId } })
  // also .override.set(body) and .override.remove({ id })
}
```

## Typed server API (server only)

```ts
// lib/gate.ts
import { createEntitlements } from "@byo-oss/entitlements"
import { upgradeTo } from "@byo-oss/entitlements/catalog"
import { auth } from "./auth"
import { catalog } from "./catalog"

// the catalog must be the plugin's catalog (same reference, else deep equal)
export const gate = createEntitlements(auth, catalog)

export async function examples(orgId: string, orgIds: string[]) {
  // → { organizationId, degraded, plan: { key, display, source: "billing"|"default"|"override" }, status, periodEnd, cancelAtPeriodEnd, features, limits, overrides: [{ kind, key, expiresAt }] }
  await gate.get(orgId)
  // ≤1000 ids; [] → []; same order
  await gate.getMany(orgIds)
  // → { allowed, reason, key, plan, upgradeTo: PlanKey[] }
  await gate.hasFeature(orgId, "exports")
  // → { key, plan, limit, allowed, reason, upgradeTo, degraded }; metered keys add { used, remaining, resetAt }; consumes nothing
  await gate.getLimit(orgId, "apiCalls")
  // metered keys only → { allowed, reason, used, limit, remaining, resetAt, firstRefusal, plan, upgradeTo }
  await gate.consumeUsage(orgId, "apiCalls", { amount: 1 })
  // capacity keys only → { allowed, reason, count, limit, over, plan, upgradeTo }
  await gate.checkCapacity(orgId, "members", { count: 4, adding: 1 })
  // resync from the source now (also refreshes a stale snapshot); THROWS on a source/db failure
  await gate.sync(orgId)
  // clear this process's cache entry
  await gate.invalidate(orgId)
  // plan keys that unlock it, in catalog order
  upgradeTo(catalog, { feature: "sso" })
  upgradeTo(catalog, { limit: "projects", atLeast: 10 })
}
```

- reason: "ok" | "not_in_plan" | "limit_reached" | "error".
- consumeUsage is one guarded incrementOne: atomic, refusals never count (used unchanged, refused +1), firstRefusal is true once per period (emits limit_reached). amount is a positive integer.
- A limit of 0 means not included: getLimit, consumeUsage and checkCapacity all answer reason "not_in_plan" (a metered refusal still counts toward refused, and the first one in a period emits limit_reached). A metered key with remaining 0 → limit_reached. upgradeTo never names the org's current plan. Results are read-only (frozen): copy before changing.
- checkCapacity: allowed = count + adding <= limit; over = count > limit (a downgraded org). Two concurrent creates can both pass checkCapacity: lock the organization row (SELECT … FOR UPDATE) in the transaction that counts and creates.
- Failure policy: reads never throw for an outage. A throwing db/source/resolveEntitlements hook → get/getMany/getLimit answer defaultPlan with degraded: true; hasFeature/consumeUsage/checkCapacity answer onError(error, { organizationId, key, operation }) ("deny" by default) with reason "error". One log line per failure. An id that is not an organization answers defaultPlan, not degraded, and writes nothing (consumeUsage refuses it with not_in_plan and creates no counter).
- Bad arguments THROW (programmer errors, never refusals; the server API types reject typos at compile time): a wrong-kind or unknown key from an untyped caller throws "[@byo-oss/entitlements] UNKNOWN_KEY: …"; an invalid amount throws "[@byo-oss/entitlements] consumeUsage: amount must be a positive integer"; an invalid count or adding throws "[@byo-oss/entitlements] checkCapacity: count and adding must be non-negative integers". Only the first carries the UNKNOWN_KEY code; the other two are plain Errors.

A 429 for a refused call:

```ts
// lib/guard.ts
import { gate } from "./gate"

export async function guardApiCall(organizationId: string): Promise<Response | null> {
  const r = await gate.consumeUsage(organizationId, "apiCalls")
  if (r.allowed) return null
  return new Response("Limit reached", {
    status: r.reason === "error" ? 503 : 429,
    headers: { "retry-after": String(Math.ceil((r.resetAt.getTime() - Date.now()) / 1000)) },
  })
}
```

## Options (every duration is in ms except pastDueGraceDays)

catalog (required) · source (BillingSource; unset → everyone on defaultPlan + overrides) · isEntitled(snapshot, now) (default: active, trialing, past_due within grace) · pastDueGraceDays 7 (days, counted from pastDueSince) · resolveEntitlements({ organizationId, plan, snapshot, features, limits }) → { features?, limits? } (replaces keys; after a plan override, before feature/limit overrides) · staffOrganizationId · authorize({ session, headers, organizationId, permissions }) · acceptSession({ session, headers, kind: "member"|"staff", method, path }) (default refuses impersonated sessions on staff calls and POSTs, and nothing else; a custom one replaces it) · onEvent(event) · onError(error, { organizationId, key, operation }) default deny · cacheTtlMs 30000 (0 = off; max 10000 orgs) · maxAge 3600000 (≥60000) · usageRetention 7776000000 (≥86400000) · overrideRetention 31536000000 (≥86400000) · organizationCleanup true · maxAttempts 5 · batchSize 100 (1-1000; one budget per sweep call, shared by its steps: resyncs, override expiry, pruning) · leaseMs 300000 · schema (rename tables/columns).

- a value in the wrong unit (overrideRetention: 365) fails boot. Boot errors are prefixed [@byo-oss/entitlements]. No organization plugin → ORGANIZATION_PLUGIN_REQUIRED. No staffOrganizationId and no authorize → one warning; override endpoints deny.
- Refusing API-key or bearer callers on the override endpoints is an app choice, not the default. A custom acceptSession keeps the impersonation rule and adds its own:

```ts
// lib/accept-session.ts
import type { EntitlementsAcceptSession } from "@byo-oss/entitlements"

export const acceptSession: EntitlementsAcceptSession = ({ session, kind, method, path, headers }) => {
  if (session.session.impersonatedBy && (kind === "staff" || method === "POST")) return false
  const bearer = headers?.get("authorization")?.startsWith("Bearer ")
  if (path.startsWith("/entitlements/override") && (bearer || headers?.has("x-api-key"))) return false
  return true
}
```

## Endpoints (all need a session; no credential-free route)

- GET /entitlements/get (getEntitlements): gated entitlements:read in organizationId, else in the staff org → result + usage per metered key { used, remaining, resetAt }; staff also see override id, reason, createdBy.
- POST /entitlements/refresh (refreshEntitlements): same gate → same body after a cache-bypassing sync (call on return from checkout).
- POST /entitlements/override/set (setEntitlementOverride): gated entitlements:override in the staff org → { override }; body { organizationId, kind: "plan"|"feature"|"limit", key, value, reason (1-500 chars), expiresAt? (future) }.
- POST /entitlements/override/remove (removeEntitlementOverride): gated entitlements:override in the staff org → { ok: true }; body { id }.
- GET /entitlements/overrides (listEntitlementOverrides): gated entitlements:read in the staff org; query { organizationId?, status?, cursor? } → { overrides, nextCursor }, newest first, up to 50 per page.
- auth.api.processEntitlementsSync({}) (server-only, no HTTP route) → { synced, skipped, retrying, failed, expired, pruned, hasMore }.

GET endpoints (for apps that classify GETs, e.g. an impersonation guard): /entitlements/get, /entitlements/overrides. Every other route is POST.

Gate order: authorize in the target org (member), else in the staff org (staff); neither → 404 ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND (never 403, no id leak); acceptSession false → 403 SESSION_NOT_ACCEPTED; staff paths check the organization exists. 503 ENTITLEMENTS_UNAVAILABLE instead of a degraded plan. Bad override → 400 INVALID_OVERRIDE; unknown override → 404 OVERRIDE_NOT_FOUND; bad list cursor → 400 INVALID_CURSOR.

Overrides replace the plan's value (they can restrict). One live plan override per org; a new override for the same (org, kind, key) marks the old one removed. A plan override has no value; its key is a plan key (not an alias).

## Billing sources

```ts
// lib/auth-stripe.ts
// needs @better-auth/stripe ^1.7.7 with subscription.enabled and organization.enabled
import Stripe from "stripe"
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"
import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins/organization"
import { stripe } from "@better-auth/stripe"
import { entitlements } from "@byo-oss/entitlements"
import { fromBetterAuthStripe, stripePlans } from "@byo-oss/entitlements/stripe"
import { ac, roles } from "./permissions"
import { catalog } from "./catalog"

export const auth = betterAuth({
  plugins: [
    organization({ ac, roles }),
    stripe({
      stripeClient: new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY!),
      stripeWebhookSecret: process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
      organization: { enabled: true },
      subscription: {
        enabled: true,
        plans: stripePlans(catalog, { pro: { priceId: process.env.STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID! } }),
      },
    }),
    entitlements({ catalog, source: fromBetterAuthStripe() }),
  ],
})
```

- Boot fails when a Stripe plan name is not a catalog plan or alias. fromBetterAuthStripe wraps the Stripe plugin's onEvent once: on checkout.session.completed and customer.subscription.created|updated|deleted it resyncs the organization, then calls your handler. Unknown/user/deleted-org events answer 200; a failed resync → 400 so Stripe redelivers. One stripe() plugin per betterAuth() instance. It only reads the subscription table.
- BillingSource: { id, resolve(organizationId, { adapter }) → BillingState | null (throw to retry; read via ctx.adapter), connect?(context, changed) }. BillingState: { planKey, status, periodStart?, periodEnd?, cancelAtPeriodEnd?, seats?, sourceRef? }. No permanent-failure type: a failing source never drops a paid plan.
- Community adapters: package byo-entitlements-<provider> (known adapters: none yet), tested with testBillingSource (vitest, ESM only). memorySource() from @byo-oss/entitlements/testing is a settable in-memory source: `await source.set(orgId, { planKey: "pro", status: "active" })`, `source.setFailure(new Error("down"))`.

```ts
// src/source.test.ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"
import { memoryAdapter } from "better-auth/adapters/memory"
import { getAuthTables } from "better-auth/db"
import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins/organization"
import { entitlements, type BillingSource, type BillingState } from "@byo-oss/entitlements"
import { defineEntitlements } from "@byo-oss/entitlements/catalog"
import { testBillingSource } from "@byo-oss/entitlements/testing"

const catalog = defineEntitlements({
  features: ["exports"],
  limits: { projects: { kind: "capacity" } },
  plans: {
    free: { features: { exports: false }, limits: { projects: 3 } },
    pro: { features: { exports: true }, limits: { projects: "unlimited" } },
  },
  defaultPlan: "free",
})

// stands in for your package's source
function createSource(states: Map<string, BillingState | null>, failing = false): BillingSource {
  return {
    id: "acme",
    async resolve(organizationId) {
      if (failing) throw new Error("provider is down")
      const state = states.get(organizationId)
      return state ? structuredClone(state) : null
    },
  }
}

async function build(source: BillingSource) {
  const options = {
    secret: "test_secret",
    emailAndPassword: { enabled: true },
    plugins: [organization(), entitlements({ catalog, source })],
  }
  // the memory adapter needs one empty array per table
  const tables: Record<string, object[]> = {}
  for (const table of Object.keys(getAuthTables(options))) tables[table] = []
  const auth = betterAuth({ ...options, database: memoryAdapter(tables) })
  const { user } = await auth.api.signUpEmail({
    body: { email: "owner@acme.test", password: "test_secret", name: "Owner" },
  })
  const created = await auth.api.createOrganization({
    body: { name: "Acme", slug: "acme", userId: user.id },
  })
  return { auth, organizationId: created.id }
}

testBillingSource({
  name: "acme source",
  setup: async () => {
    const states = new Map<string, BillingState | null>()
    const source = createSource(states)
    return {
      source,
      ...(await build(source)),
      setState: async (organizationId, state) => {
        states.set(organizationId, state)
      },
    }
  },
  failing: async () => {
    const source = createSource(new Map(), true)
    return { source, ...(await build(source)) }
  },
})
```

## Freshness

- push (source events) · read-through (first read writes a snapshot, also with no subscription) · background refresh past maxAge (context.runInBackground when advanced.backgroundTasks.handler is set, else marked due for the sweep) · sweep · refreshEntitlements after checkout.
- The sweep claims due snapshots with a lease, resolves, backs off 1 min doubling (cap maxAge), marks overrides past expiresAt "expired", prunes usage (usageRetention) and ended overrides (overrideRetention). After maxAttempts a snapshot counts failed, keeps its last good state and retries at maxAge. Without a source only expiry and pruning run. @byo-oss/core's sweepAll(auth) runs it with the other BYO plugins.
- Delivery: sweeps are at-least-once. A lease that expires (leaseMs) while a slow sweep is still working lets a second sweep claim the same row and both resync it; harmless, because a resync writes absolute state. Syncs write absolute state; events are best-effort, at most once, in-process.
- Staleness across processes: each process caches up to cacheTtlMs (30s); it clears its own entry on its own writes and on invalidate(). Another process's write can show up cacheTtlMs late. refreshEntitlements returns the latest state: a lost concurrent write is retried up to 3 times, then it answers 503 ENTITLEMENTS_UNAVAILABLE (a Stripe push that loses the same way answers 400, so Stripe redelivers). Usage counters are never cached.
- incrementOne atomicity: Kysely/Drizzle re-apply the guard on the UPDATE from better-auth 1.7.7 (exact); memory, Prisma, MongoDB native (exact); a custom adapter without incrementOne uses core's fallback (prior-value guard, 5 tries, then throws → onError denies under contention).

```ts
// scripts/cron.ts (server only; run every minute)
import { auth } from "../lib/auth"

export async function sweep(): Promise<void> {
  let more = true
  while (more) {
    const result = await auth.api.processEntitlementsSync({})
    more = result.hasMore
  }
}
```

## Inside a transaction (adapters with real transactions)

- Everything reads/writes through getCurrentAdapter, so a call in your runWithTransaction joins it.
- get/getMany/hasFeature/getLimit/checkCapacity work: they never write the cache, never persist a snapshot, never schedule a refresh.
- consumeUsage, sync(orgId) and refreshEntitlements THROW "[@byo-oss/entitlements] <name> must run outside a transaction": call them before/after.
- processEntitlementsSync, byo.sweep and @byo-oss/core's sweepAll JOIN the transaction and roll back with it: the sweep only updates and deletes existing rows, so it cannot abort the caller's transaction with a create conflict. Their plan.changed events are emitted before the caller commits.
- Inside a joined transaction the cache entry is cleared before the commit, so a read made outside the transaction in that window can re-cache the old state until cacheTtlMs. Override writes made inside a transaction behave the same way.
- On Postgres, a database error inside a joined sweep aborts the caller's transaction: the sweep call rejects (it does not report retrying) and the caller's commit then fails. Run sweeps outside app transactions unless you want them to roll back together.
- Override writes join the transaction too and roll back with it.
- Events fire when the adapter write returns, not after commit: the public better-auth entry exports no after-commit hook, so in 0.1.0 an event emitted inside a caller's transaction (an override write, a sweep) can announce a write that rolls back. After-commit is a follow-up.

## Events (onEvent; best-effort, at most once, in-process; no free text)

- entitlements.plan.changed { from, to, status }: snapshot writes only. Overrides never emit it, so a plan override changes the resolved plan without this event.
- entitlements.override.set { kind, key, value, expiresAt }
- entitlements.override.removed { kind, key } (expiry emits nothing)
- entitlements.usage.limit_reached { key, limit, periodEnd } (first refusal per period)

To notify owners, call auth.api.notify. It exists only when @byo-oss/notifications is installed and inbox() is in plugins. Use the event type as the notification type (SPEC P2).

```ts
// lib/auth-notify.ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"
import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins/organization"
import { inbox } from "@byo-oss/notifications"
import { entitlements } from "@byo-oss/entitlements"
import { catalog } from "./catalog"

export const auth = betterAuth({
  plugins: [
    organization(),
    inbox(),
    entitlements({
      catalog,
      // annotate the return type so TypeScript doesn't infer `auth` from itself
      onEvent: async (event): Promise<void> => {
        if (event.type !== "entitlements.usage.limit_reached") return
        await auth.api.notify({
          body: {
            organizationId: event.organizationId,
            roles: ["owner", "admin"],
            type: event.type,
            title: `You reached your ${event.data.key} limit`,
            href: "/billing",
          },
        })
      },
    }),
  ],
})
```

## React (@byo-oss/entitlements/react; pass the client as a prop)

```tsx
// components/exports.tsx
import { EntitlementGate, UsageMeter, useEntitlements } from "@byo-oss/entitlements/react"
import { authClient } from "../lib/auth-client"
import { catalog } from "../lib/catalog"

export function Exports({ organizationId }: { organizationId: string }) {
  // → { data, isLoading, error, hasFeature(key), limit(key), usage(key), refresh() }
  const entitlements = useEntitlements<typeof catalog>({ client: authClient, organizationId })
  return (
    <>
      <EntitlementGate
        entitlements={entitlements}
        feature="exports"
        catalog={catalog}
        fallback={({ upgradeTo, isLoading }) =>
          isLoading ? null : <a href="/billing">Upgrade to {upgradeTo[0]}</a>
        }
      >
        <button type="button">Export</button>
      </EntitlementGate>
      {/* role="progressbar", aria-valuenow/min/max/valuetext ("920 of 1,000 API calls used today"), shadcn tokens */}
      <UsageMeter
        entitlements={entitlements}
        limitKey="apiCalls"
        catalog={catalog}
        className="w-48"
        barClassName="h-2"
        labels={{ loading: "Loading usage", error: "Usage unavailable" }}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

Tailwind v4 skips node_modules: add `@source "<path>/node_modules/@byo-oss/entitlements/dist";` to the CSS file that imports Tailwind.

## Lifecycle, export, uninstall

- organizationCleanup (default true) deletes an org's rows after /organization/delete. organizationCleanup: false → SQL cascades via FKs, memory/MongoDB keep rows until you call deleteOrganizationData. User delete nulls createdBy/removedBy on overrides.
- To run the cleanup yourself (SPEC 6.2), turn the automatic one off and wire deleteOrganizationData into the organization plugin's hook. Use it when you want the cleanup under your control or turned the automatic hook off; for deletes that never go through the organization plugin call deleteOrganizationData directly (purgeOrganization below).

```ts
// lib/auth-cleanup.ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"
import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins/organization"
import { deleteOrganizationData, entitlements } from "@byo-oss/entitlements"
import { catalog } from "./catalog"

export const auth = betterAuth({
  plugins: [
    organization({
      organizationHooks: {
        // annotate the return type so TypeScript doesn't infer `auth` from itself
        afterDeleteOrganization: async ({ organization }): Promise<void> => {
          await deleteOrganizationData(auth, organization.id)
        },
      },
    }),
    entitlements({ catalog, organizationCleanup: false }),
  ],
})
```

- exportEntitlementsData: limit 1-1000; offset paging over id, so a row deleted mid-export can shift later rows; one model per page (page.snapshots, page.overrides with createdByEmail and removedByEmail, page.usage). The catalog is not exported.
- Uninstall: remove the plugin, then drop entitlementUsage, entitlementOverride, entitlementSnapshot (in that order; none references another).

```ts
// scripts/lifecycle.ts (server only)
import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises"
import { deleteOrganizationData, exportEntitlementsData } from "@byo-oss/entitlements"
import { auth } from "../lib/auth"

// for deletes made outside /organization/delete
export async function purgeOrganization(organizationId: string): Promise<void> {
  await deleteOrganizationData(auth, organizationId)
}

export async function exportOrganization(organizationId: string): Promise<void> {
  let cursor: string | null = null
  let n = 0
  do {
    const page = await exportEntitlementsData(auth, { organizationId, cursor, limit: 100 })
    await writeFile(`entitlements-${n++}.json`, JSON.stringify(page))
    cursor = page.nextCursor
  } while (cursor)
}
```

## Notes

- schema: entitlementSnapshot (organizationId unique; planKey, status, periodStart/End, cancelAtPeriodEnd, seats, pastDueSince, sourceRef, version, syncedAt, nextSyncAt, syncState, syncClaimedAt, syncAttempts, syncError), entitlementOverride (organizationId, status, kind, key, value JSON, reason, permanent, expiresAt, endedAt, createdBy, removedBy, createdAt), entitlementUsage (bucket unique, organizationId, key, periodStart, periodEnd, used, refused). Full tables in the README.
- MongoDB: create unique indexes on entitlementSnapshot.organizationId and entitlementUsage.bucket, or concurrent first writes can duplicate rows and over-allow.
- Error codes: ENTITLEMENTS_ERROR_CODES (ORGANIZATION_PLUGIN_REQUIRED, NOT_ALLOWED, SESSION_NOT_ACCEPTED, UNKNOWN_KEY, INVALID_OVERRIDE, OVERRIDE_NOT_FOUND, ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND, ENTITLEMENTS_UNAVAILABLE, INVALID_CURSOR).
- Do not query or write the plugin's tables from app code; go through createEntitlements, auth.api.*, the client and the exported functions.
- community plugin, not affiliated with better-auth
